note: The public version ladder. Each rung has a short `phase` name and a `summary`, both written for this site. `scripts/check-ladder.mjs` checks every row against the plan: the same version, the same state, and a `phase` that names the same phase. States: done, planned, goal, later.

rungs.summary: The foundation: the plugin loads as CLAP, VST3 and AU and as a standalone app, asks you to accept its licence, and opens on an 88-key keyboard with every key named.
The real pianos: Grand, Acoustic, Upright and Honky-Tonk, their keys moving and sounding as they play.

rungs.phase: Phase 2 — Realistic Hands at the Keyboard
rungs.summary: Realistic hands at the keyboard, fingering every note the way a pianist would, with sixty-two public-domain classics to learn and a transport to scrub through them.
Generate in any style, read the four sheets as they light up, and drag the MIDI into your DAW.
The overhead and side views, with the sheets lying flat on the piano, and a seamless switch between views.
Lessons from Day 1: a piano course that listens to you play and moves on when you have it right, and a Read Aloud switch that reads each lesson to you, each word lit as it is spoken.
A mixer for every part, with faders, pan, EQ, effects and compression, and drags that keep the mix.
The Song view: build a whole song from sections by hand, or start from an artist's or a genre's arrangement, then watch it played and drag it out.
More courses: reading sheet music, rhythm, ear training, music theory with the Nashville Number System, songwriting and lyrics, arranging, and mixing.
Finger drumming on a pad controller whose pads light up with every hit, from the first beat to full grooves.
A drum kit set up and played the way a professional drummer would, and a drum machine beside it, with one switch to choose which plays your drums.
Live listening: play a real instrument or sing into a microphone or an instrument cable, and the lessons hear it, with a tuner and latency calibration.
The guitars: steel-string, nylon, electric and muted, fretted, picked and strummed by a guitarist's hands, with TAB on the sheets and two guitar courses.
The bass guitar, played with the fingers and slapped.
Your own audio and MIDI, read into parts and played by the hands.
The classics: public-domain tunes to watch and listen to.
The realism pass: lighting, materials and motion held to filmed playing.
The finish: settings, eighteen languages throughout, accessibility and the manual.
Update notices and the trial and paid editions.

rungs.phase: Phase 12 — Release Candidate & the First Public Release
rungs.summary: The first public release.
Electric pianos and organs, the organs with a pedalboard for the bassline.

rungs.phase: Phase 14 — The Keys Family II & More Frets
rungs.summary: Harpsichord, clavinet, celesta and toy piano; ukulele, banjo and mandolin.
The mallets: xylophone, marimba, vibraphone and glockenspiel.

rungs.phase: Phase 16 — The Harp & More Plucked Strings
rungs.summary: The harp, koto, sitar and mountain dulcimer.
Violin, viola, cello and double bass, bowed and plucked.
Flute, clarinet, saxophones, oboe and recorder.
Trumpet, trombone, French horn and tuba.
Play along and learn mode.
The band: every part on its own instrument, each with its own player.
